text: Sourdough fermentation depends on a stable community of wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria. The starter is maintained by discarding a portion of the culture and refreshing it with flour and water at regular intervals, which keeps the population in an exponential growth phase. Hydration is expressed as a baker's percentage relative to flour weight, and a wetter starter ferments faster because diffusion of nutrients through the matrix is less restricted. Temperature is the dominant variable: below eighteen degrees the bacteria outpace the yeast and the culture turns sour without rising.

Espresso extraction is governed by the interaction of grind size, dose, and pressure. Water at approximately ninety-three degrees is forced through a compacted bed of coffee at nine bars. Finer grinds increase surface area and resistance, extending contact time; coarser grinds allow channelling, where water finds a path of least resistance and leaves much of the bed under-extracted. Ratio is conventionally expressed as the mass of liquid out divided by the mass of dry coffee in.

The tempering of chocolate is a controlled crystallisation. Cocoa butter can solidify into six polymorphic forms, only one of which produces the desired snap and gloss. The chocolate is melted, cooled while agitated to seed the correct crystal form, then gently rewarmed to melt the unstable forms without destroying the seeds. Insufficient tempering produces bloom, a dull grey surface where fat has migrated and recrystallised.

Stock is an extraction of collagen and aromatic compounds into water. Bones are simmered rather than boiled, because agitation emulsifies fat into the liquid and clouds it. Collagen converts to gelatin over several hours, which is what gives a finished stock body when chilled. Aromatics are added late, since their volatile compounds are driven off by prolonged heat.

Bread staling is not primarily loss of moisture but retrogradation: the recrystallisation of gelatinised starch as it cools. This is why a stale loaf can be partly refreshed by heating, which re-melts the crystals, and why refrigeration accelerates staling while freezing arrests it. Crumb structure depends on gluten development, which aligns protein strands into an elastic network capable of retaining fermentation gases.
